must_remember: The Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics provides the logical foundation for the existence of temperature as a universal property shared by systems in thermal equilibrium.
The absolute temperature $T$ of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the average translational kinetic energy per molecule: $E_{avg} = \frac{3}{2} k_B T$.
The Kelvin scale sets its zero at absolute zero ($-273.15^{\circ}\text{C}$) and uses the triple point of water ($273.16\text{ K}$) as its single defining fixed point.
The thermodynamic temperature scale is independent of the specific thermometric substance or property used to measure it.
Heat flows spontaneously from a body at a higher temperature to one at a lower temperature, governed strictly by temperature gradients rather than total thermal energy.

glossary.meaning: A wall that allows thermal energy (heat) to pass freely between two thermodynamic systems.
A state in which two systems in thermal contact do not undergo any changes in macroscopic properties over time.
The theoretical temperature limit ($0\text{ K}$ or $-273.15^{\circ}\text{C}$) at which the entropy of a pure crystalline substance vanishes.
The single temperature and pressure ($273.16\text{ K}$ and $0.01^{\circ}\text{C}$) at which ice, liquid water, and water vapor coexist in equilibrium.
A theorem stating that in thermal equilibrium, energy is shared equally among all active degrees of freedom, each contributing $\frac{1}{2}k_BT$ per molecule.
